newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise in week to Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise in week to Dec 13.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of December 13 were $5.212 billion, compared to $5.015 billion on December 6.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of the same date were $16.344 billion, compared to $16.398 billion as of December 13.
It said the increase of $197 million in international assets in the week was due to:
- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) worth $144 million
- Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $41 million

- A net gain of $12 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose by 10.442 billion pesos due to a seasonal rise in demand for notes and coins, with many Christmas bonuses paid in the last week.
"This demand is expected to continue rising this week, and a considerable reduction is expected to be seen in the last week of December," the central bank said.
The balance of the federal government's deposits with the central bank fell by 13.209 billion pesos, mainly as a result of transfers of funds to state governments.
Central bank credit to financial institutions fell by 2.956 billion pesos to compensate for the monetary impact of the increase in assets and the withdrawal of funds by the federal government.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
